notes.problem: The 'peeled curl' is a rigid rectangular tab with a hard wedge of shadow, and both footer lines sit on the holder rail and the notched card.
notes.fix: Model the free end as a thin strip on a curve that lifts toward the camera, and raise the camera target about 50 mm so the card bottoms and holder sit above native y 2400 and the footer lands on dark ledge.

notes.problem: The tape's free end is a rigid rectangular stub with a hard near-black wedge, not a peel, and the footer lines sit on the holder rail and card corner.
notes.fix: Model the free end as a curved peel bending 40 to 60 degrees toward the camera with a soft curl, and raise the camera target about 50 mm so the holder rails clear native y 2400 and both footer lines sit on the dark ledge.

notes.problem: The close is the cover reshot closer, and the planned peeling curl renders as a rigid flat red bar jutting horizontally past the card edge. It reads as a printed stick, not tape, and the image adds nothing new to the argument.
notes.fix: Model the tape as a thin lofted ribbon whose free end lifts and curls toward the camera with its pale underside showing and a soft cast on the card face. Or replace the frame with frame 3's tray camera, the taped card back in the front slot, so the close is a new state of the motif.

notes.problem: The two stacks read as flat beige boxes with smeared top sheets. The slid notched and plain top pair can't be read, the stack faces sit in the mid tones, and the horizon tilts.
notes.fix: Drop the key so it rakes the stack edges into fine card lines, slide the top pair forward until the clipped corner is silhouetted against the dark ledge, level the horizon, and tighten the pool so the stack fronts fall off to black.

notes.problem: The stacks read as cardboard boxes, not cards. The slid top pairs drape like sheets and hide the notch, a jagged black shadow artifact sits on the left stack's right face, and the ledge horizon slices through the dek's last line.
notes.fix: Rebuild each stack as instanced rounded card boxes with every tenth card offset, and lay the slid pair flat and square so the notched corner faces the camera. Lower the camera target so the horizon falls below the dek, and tighten the shadow camera bounds to remove the jagged artifact.

notes.problem: The top sheets on both stacks float and clip over the block, a dark wedge cuts into the left stack, and the notched-card pair the dossier requires can't be seen. A wide dead dark zone sits between the stacks.
notes.fix: Lay the slid top pair as two separate solid cards resting on the stack tops, with the notched corner turned to camera. Push the camera in so the two stacks fill two thirds of the width, and let the key rake the instanced edges.

notes.problem: The drawer runs off the right edge, so the 100 cards behind 'nearly 10 in 100' can't be counted. The grit is uniform in density and size and sits close to the ember hue.
notes.fix: Shift the drawer about 120 mm left in world space with the same camera so the end wall and last block return to frame, and cut the grit by two thirds with mixed sizes, falloff with distance, and a desaturated grey-brown.

notes.problem: Uniform warm grit reads as confetti across the middle band. The drawer runs off the right edge so the hundred can't be counted, the plain card faces turn grey away from the key, and the drawer front is a broad flat brown slab. The art review's repair was never applied.
notes.fix: Apply the review's own repair in one render: shift the drawer about 120 mm left so its end wall and last tab are in frame, cut the grit density by two thirds with mixed sizes and distance fade, and rotate the card blocks about 15 degrees into the key so their faces read bone.

notes.problem: Orange speckle scattered over the far ground reads as render noise. The drawer front is a large flat dead plane, and the flagged block, the frame's whole point, is small at the far left.
notes.fix: Remove the scatter so the ground beyond the pool falls to black. Raise and swing the camera so the flagged block of cards sits large at centre-left, with the drawer front cropped off the bottom edge.

notes.problem: The card face fills the lower half in flat mid tone, its ruled lines run straight through the c19 and texasaidocket.com footer, and the neutral wording is at 23px, under the mobile floor.
notes.fix: Crop the card so its bottom edge ends above the footer band with the pool falling to black across the lower card, and set the neutral line at 24px or larger.

notes.problem: There is a dead dark band about 300 display px tall between the dek and the card. The card face is an evenly lit mid-tone field that falls to black by vignette, not by light, and the neutral wording is set at 23 px, under the 24 px floor (machine_qa warn).
notes.fix: Raise the card about 250 px to close the band, and drop the key elevation so it rakes low across the face, letting the debossed lines and the tape's lifted corner cast visibly. Set the neutral line at 24 px or more.

notes.problem: The bone card is a near-flat mid-tone plate filling half the frame, the tape barely stands proud at feed size, and the neutral wording is set at 23 px, under the 24 px floor.
notes.fix: Set the neutral line at 26 px or more. Tilt the relief toward the key with a sharper falloff and lift the tape's near corner, so it casts a visible shadow and the card face drops toward black at its edges.

notes.problem: The txbench relief reads as a flat horizontal bar chart: ten strips with almost no visible height or cast, in a wide mid-tone pool on a neutral black ground that leaves the deck's navy and ledge world, with labels placed like axis names. It also fuses the preprint's 10-condition count with the release's highlights.
notes.fix: Stand the card on the shale ledge in the lastLight world with the key raking from the right at a low angle, so each strip throws a visibly offset cast and its curled end lifts. Tighten the pool so the card's lower half falls to black, and drive the strip count from a published-study figure or drop the count entirely.

notes.problem: Reads as a horizontal bar chart in a vignette spotlight. No card edge or notch is visible, the left half is a dead mid-brown field holding the labels, the strips' casts are hairlines (cast_fraction 0.018), and the 'curled right ends' are torn flat ends.
notes.fix: Render it as a spatial frame through txthree at the cover's key (az 62, el 14): the whole notched card lies on the shale, cropped only at the bottom. Model the ten strips with lifted, curled right ends so each throws a long cast to the left, and put the two labels on the dark ledge beside the card instead of a lit mid-tone panel.

notes.problem: Seventeen small rings scattered on an empty ledge, with no dominant silhouette and about 60 percent of the image area empty dark ground. They read as napkin rings, the lower band edges render jagged, and the ember tab in the storyboard's motif list is missing, so the motif breaks.
notes.fix: Drop the camera to about 0.06 m with fov about 18 so the three rows fill about 70 percent of the width as one grouped mass. Model each band as a flat vinyl strip with a label panel and the ember tab, and raise the band geometry's segment count and shadow bias to clean up the ragged lower edges.

notes.problem: The 17 'wristbands' read as crescent rings with jagged, aliased rims. They sit in a low strip and leave the frame's middle third empty, so a reader sees rings, not hospital bands.
notes.fix: Model each band as a flat strap with a tail and a visible snap, lying on its side rather than standing as a hoop. Raise the segment count to kill the jaggies, and enlarge the three rows until they fill the lower half.

notes.problem: The turn frame is nearly identical to slide 3. The moved taped card sits in the back slot almost entirely hidden by the front card, so the one change the deck turns on is about a strip of tape at 432 px.
notes.fix: Raise the back slot or lift the moved card so the taped notched card clears the front card by about half its height, and drop the other two trays out of the pool so the moved card is the only lit thing in the frame.
